thread:
elaine: Quick thought — for the form on Deployments, should we show field-level errors as users interact, or a single summary banner that lists all problems after submit? Inline is faster for fixing but gets noisy on multi-section forms. :thinking_face:

sam: I lean inline for immediacy. For multi-row/bulk flows a summary with anchors to each row feels less overwhelming.

vik: Inline + subtle motion works. If we go inline, use polite aria-live for incremental messages and ensure error text doesn't push layout too much. Minimal CSS idea:
````css
.input--required::after { content: '*'; opacity: .6; margin-left:4px }
.error { transform: translateY(2px); transition: transform .12s ease }
````

jo: Accessibility note: when submit fails, focus should move to the first invalid field and screen readers should get an assertive announcement for the summary. Inline-only is fine if we maintain aria-invalid and aria-describedby for each message. Also don’t rely on color alone — add icons or text.

karen: On destructive confirmations: for bulk delete, is typed-confirm (`type DELETE`) required, or is a checkbox + disabled confirm button enough? Typed confirm blocks automation but is high friction.

elaine: Proposal: item-level deletes => simple modal with a checkbox "I understand" + disabled confirm button until checked. Org-level or irreversible operations => typed-confirm. Keeps friction where risk is highest.

sam: Sounds reasonable. We should document thresholds for "org-level" so it's consistent.

vik: Also, avoid showing both a toast and inline messages for the same submission error. Pick one primary affordance; fallback messages should be deduplicated.

jo: If we use a top banner summary, include a "jump to first error" link and list items that anchor to fields (keyboard focusable). Banner should have role="alert" and link targets need clear labels.

elaine: Copy nit: instead of boring "This field is required", maybe use friendlier copy like "Please enter a value". It feels less robotic.

karen: "Please enter a value" is friendly but verbose for compact layouts. Maybe use short label + hint pattern: "Required — please enter a value" so screen readers get context and sighted users see a short badge.

sam: We can A/B test 'Required' vs 'Please enter a value' for completion on small flows.

ux-bot: Figma link created by elaine: https://figma.com/file/xyz — mock of inline errors + banner summary (comment thread started).

elaine: I'll mock both flows: (A) inline with focus jump and (B) banner summary with skip link. Vik — can you prototype the disabled-confirm + checkbox pattern and the typed-confirm variant?

vik: Yep. I'll drop a PR with markup, a11y attributes annotated, and a small demo page.

jo: I'll draft an a11y checklist: focus movement, aria-live regions, role=alert for banners, proper `aria-invalid`, keyboard-only user paths, and tests for screen reader verbosity.

sam: One more product detail — do we keep visible required markers on every field, or only on required ones? I vote for only show on required fields to reduce visual clutter.

elaine: Agreed, only on required. Also let's use a lighter-weight marker (ghost asterisk) and pair it with the hint copy for clarity.

karen: Quick dev question — for the focus-jump behaviour, should we scroll the field into view or just focus it? Mobile scrolling has weird behavior.

jo: Prefer focus + `element.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest' })` on mobile to avoid forcing large jumps. Also announce summary before moving focus so screen reader users hear there are errors.

elaine: Great. Action items: I’ll attach mocks, Vik will prototype, Jo will produce checklist, Sam will set up A/B test for copy. Reconvene after PR + mock review. :thumbsup:
